origins.section: 11.2 Only an Echo Proves the Host Is Answering
11.3 A Sign-On Belongs to One Connection
11.4 A Pool Uses a Link Only While It Is Signed On
11.6 The Host's Own Echo Is a Request, and Someone Must Answer It

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-frozen-application: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-frozen-application: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-frozen-application: Section 11.2 decides b: with keep-alive yes, the hung host's ASCIIChannel answers the empty frames in its own read loop, so the read timeout seldom fires, isConnected stays true, and the echoes expire (rx_expired=8). The page adds that every purchase sent in that time would also have expired.
recorded.prompt:q-busy-manager-thread: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-busy-manager-thread: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-busy-manager-thread: Section 11.3 describes this exact case: one unanswered exchange blocks the loop for 30 seconds while the adaptor reconnects. The boolean 'still says signed on about a connection that never was', so a is decided.
recorded.prompt:q-enabled-written-as-true: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-enabled-written-as-true: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-enabled-written-as-true: Section 11.4 says that with Boolean.TRUE the link is never used, and every purchase waits its full timeout and comes back null without leaving the pool. That decides d.
recorded.prompt:q-host-checks-the-link: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-host-checks-the-link: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-host-checks-the-link: Section 11.6 decides c: without a listener, the host's 0800/301 goes to <unhandled> and expires there, neither QMUX nor the channel answers it, and the host drops the link.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-frozen-application:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-frozen-application:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-frozen-application:a: Section 11.2 shows that the hung application answers nothing: each echo returns null and expires. Only the channel below it answers the empty frames, so no declines come back.
recorded.prompt:q-frozen-application:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-frozen-application:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-frozen-application:c: Section 11.2 says the answered empty frames mean the read timeout 'seldom saw five seconds of silence', so the link is not closed after the read timeout.
recorded.prompt:q-frozen-application:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-frozen-application:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-frozen-application:d: The 11.2 table says a TCP keep-alive answer proves only that the far side's TCP stack is there, and the probes often start after two hours. They do not detect a frozen application.
recorded.prompt:q-busy-manager-thread:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-busy-manager-thread:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-busy-manager-thread:b: The intro and 11.1 say that nothing in jPOS 2.1.7 sends a sign-on, so the adaptor does not repeat one.
recorded.prompt:q-busy-manager-thread:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-busy-manager-thread:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-busy-manager-thread:c: Section 11.3 says the flag is cleared only 'when the manager sees the link down', and 11.10 contrasts manager fields with Space entries. So a reconnect does not clear the flag through the Space.
recorded.prompt:q-busy-manager-thread:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-busy-manager-thread:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-busy-manager-thread:d: Sections 11.3 and 11.10 give expiry only to Space entries written with a lifetime, and the page never says a manager field expires. So a short inference refutes the claim that the boolean expires.
recorded.prompt:q-enabled-written-as-true:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-enabled-written-as-true:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-enabled-written-as-true:a: The 11.8 MUXPool table says that with check-enabled and one ready name, the test is enabled == the ready entry. A mere 'exists' check applies only to several ready names.
recorded.prompt:q-enabled-written-as-true:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-enabled-written-as-true:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-enabled-written-as-true:b: Section 11.4 says 'TRUE is never the ready Date', so the value matches no connection.
recorded.prompt:q-enabled-written-as-true:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-enabled-written-as-true:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-enabled-written-as-true:c: Section 11.4 says each purchase 'waits its full timeout and comes back null', not that it fails at once.
recorded.prompt:q-host-checks-the-link:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-host-checks-the-link:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-host-checks-the-link:a: Section 11.6 says the host drops the link when its own echoes go unanswered and shows them landing on <unhandled>, so the client's separate echoes answer none of them. This takes a short inference, because the page never says outright that client echoes don't count.
recorded.prompt:q-host-checks-the-link:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-host-checks-the-link:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-host-checks-the-link:b: Section 11.6 says 'Neither QMUX nor the channel answers an 0800 by itself', and 11.2 limits the channel's own answers to empty frames.
recorded.prompt:q-host-checks-the-link:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-host-checks-the-link:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-host-checks-the-link:d: Section 11.6 says QMUX puts an unmatched message on the listeners or <unhandled> and does not answer an 0800 by itself, so it sends back no error.
